records.question: Otto-kun was able to use Al Dona and such after receiving mana from the forest, but could a normal person fire off massive spells like that just from being given mana? Or did the mysterious power of the forest teach him how to use it, or did something related to his Blessing of the Soul of Language allow him to understand how to do it?
records.answerSnippet: It’s not so much that he received mana, as he was allowed to use the mana that had been allowed to build up. In short, the power of a spell changes based on the amount of mana you can use, so with ...
records.answerSearchText: It’s not so much that he received mana, as he was allowed to use the mana that had been allowed to build up. In short, the power of a spell changes based on the amount of mana you can use, so with sufficient mana, even Subaru could use Ul Shamak. He could have (past tense).

records.question: Wilhelm was moving in superhuman ways while wielding his sword, is that done with magic or using magic power? If it’s not, could Subaru move like that if he trained with the sword for decades?
records.answerSnippet: Warriors use the mana in their bodies to support them in combat, sort of like fighting spirit. It’s not done consciously, more like the mana responds to what they want to do. So, although Subaru co...
records.answerSearchText: Warriors use the mana in their bodies to support them in combat, sort of like fighting spirit. It’s not done consciously, more like the mana responds to what they want to do. So, although Subaru could manage a certain level of it, he doesn’t love the sword enough to throw half his life into it, and he wasn’t blessed with sword talent, so it’s probably impossible. Wilhelm humbly says that he lacks any talent, but a person with no talent could not have defeated a Sword Saint through effort alone. In this world, differences because of inborn talent are fairly severe.

records.question: It’s one thing for Subaru’s Shamak work on a badly injured human-form Garfiel, but why would it work on beastform Garfiel?

records.answerSearchText: It’s the opposite. It wouldn’t have worked on human-form Garfiel. Beastform Garfiel is so much dumber that it works. Not only is Garfiel a half-beast, he didn’t properly learn the beastform method from his parent, so when he goes beastform, he becomes stupid. Ram took advantage of that as well to beat him up.

records.question: Elsa was affected by even Subaru’s level of Shamak, but does that mean that Elsa has a weakness to magic? Julius said that there wasn’t a single member of the royal guard that would be affected by Subaru’s Shamak, so does that mean the royal guard has high magic resistance?
records.answerSnippet: I’m afraid you won’t be satisfied with my answer, but Elsa is terribly weak against magic. Enough that she takes pains to have anti-magic strategies. Having said that, she really wasn’t fully affec...
records.answerSearchText: I’m afraid you won’t be satisfied with my answer, but Elsa is terribly weak against magic. Enough that she takes pains to have anti-magic strategies. Having said that, she really wasn’t fully affected by Subaru’s Shamak. She simply didn’t deliberately charge through where she couldn’t see what was ahead of her. The royal guard are fairly good at using magic, but Julius was expecting a little too much of the people around him. Julius is strict with himself and others.

records.question: Elsa, who has enough power to go toe-to-toe with Garfiel, was outwitted by Subaru-kun in Arc 1, but wasn’t she just playing with him there? It looked like he was able to move around alright, so I really didn’t expect him to be in such bad shape afterwards.
records.answerSnippet: She was playing around enough that he did manage to land a kick, wasn’t she. Elsa is similar to a saiyan in that as she faces stronger opponents, she becomes stronger herself, so when she was facin...
records.answerSearchText: She was playing around enough that he did manage to land a kick, wasn’t she. Elsa is similar to a saiyan in that as she faces stronger opponents, she becomes stronger herself, so when she was facing Subaru-kun, it turns out like that. (Note: ‘saiyan’ is a Dragonball reference.)

records.question: I think that Shamak is a smokescreen-style magic, but why is Al Shamak able to interfere with other dimensions? What kind of relationship does it have with that spell name?
records.answerSnippet: The “Shamak” line isn’t a smokescreen, it breaks the connection between the mind and body of targets in it’s radius. With Shamak, the body loses it’s perception. With El Shamak, the body becomes un...
records.answerSearchText: The “Shamak” line isn’t a smokescreen, it breaks the connection between the mind and body of targets in it’s radius. With Shamak, the body loses it’s perception. With El Shamak, the body becomes unable to be controlled. With Ul Shamak, the mind gets tossed out (literally: the mind gets German Suplexed). With Al Shamak, the body gets sent to another world along with it.

records.answerSnippet: A color appropriate to the affinity is bestowed as a title on those who reach the pinnacle of a particular affinity. In Lugunica, “Blue” is Ferris, “Red” and “Green” and “Yellow” are all held toget...
records.answerSearchText: A color appropriate to the affinity is bestowed as a title on those who reach the pinnacle of a particular affinity. In Lugunica, “Blue” is Ferris, “Red” and “Green” and “Yellow” are all held together by Roswaal. “Black” and “White” are absent. There’s currently no title for the strongest magic user, but it would be “Great Sorcerer”.
